key_insight: Disk-like droplets with high circularity and expansion promote dense, fine-lamellar Fe-based amorphous coatings, while greater porosity reduces long-term corrosion resistance.
engineering_relevance: Optimizing detonation-spray parameters to limit porosity and accounting for operating humidity can improve coating durability on carbon-steel components.
method: Deposited Fe-based amorphous coatings on Q235 carbon steel using varied detonation-spray parameters.
Examined droplet morphology and coating microstructure.
Evaluated long-term corrosion and wear under different humidity conditions using Si3N4 counterface balls.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports poorer long-term corrosion resistance with higher porosity and decreasing friction coefficient and wear rate as humidity increased.
watch_item: Humidity-dependent wear findings involve Si3N4–water tribochemistry and may not transfer directly to other counterface materials.
paper_title: Long-term corrosion behaviors and wear behavior of Fe-based amorphous coatings in different humidity environments
